mascot.name: Pip
mascot.design: An original baby elephant, about the size the reference cat reads at (70-90 px tall in card-local units). Bean-shaped body, four short column legs with three cream toenail arcs each, ONE big D-shaped ear (the emotion dial: perked = alert, flared = startled, droopy = sad, folded over the eyes = scared), a short trunk with a curl at the tip and three ink wrinkle ticks (our answer to the cat's stripes), a tiny tufted tail, a single dot eye, no tusks, no clothes, no text on the body. Hand-inked outline in theme ink with small overshoots; flat fill slightly misregistered like the rest of the art. Usually seen side-on or three-quarter-back, watching the explanation like the cat does; faces camera exactly once (S04 'right?'). Trunk gestures carry the gags: curl to mouth = 'shh', crossed trunk = 'fingers crossed', raised = pose-match / yawn, tapping = testing a padlock. Differs from the official elePHPant: rounder and smaller, single visible ear, no logo, no 'php' lettering.
mascot.colorway: Periwinkle, matching src/lib/mascot/colors.ts (body #8D90CC, shade #7377B5, earInner palette.salmon, cheek palette.salmon, nails palette.cream, ink palette.ink). Color code taught by the video: periwinkle = PHP. It is used ONLY for Pip and for the small elephant cornerstone emblems / PHP markers (S02 tally, S10 dots, S12 emblems). Orange stays reserved for the sun and the 'attention' accents, peach for highlights and the patch. Pip is therefore the single cool-violet shape in every frame, so the eye finds him instantly without him competing with the orange disc.

scenes.vo: Government websites in four countries just switched themselves off. Nobody hacked them.
scenes.title: Four capitols power down

transitionIn.notes: Frame 0 is the exact frame the S13 un-build ends on: complete ink linework of this plaza, mint sky block, orange sun with a faint (60% cream) power glyph, periwinkle Pip, no other fills, empty caption zone. Fills flood in on the first word so the very first half-second already moves.

Plaza paving in light perspective y 905-1095 (mintPale), lamp posts at x 120 and x 840 (y 760-1050), five back-view citizens x 300-560 y 975-1070. A phone/power wire with three pigeons spans x 70-890 at y ~250 between the back buildings. Pip on the plaza x 680-760 y 990-1070 facing the buildings. Palette: facades cream/peach/tan, columns cream, glass mintPale, doors and shutters teal/tealDark, pennants salmon/teal/sage/brown, orange only in the sun.

beats.action: Frame 0 = loop seam: linework + sky + sun (faint power glyph) + Pip only. Slow camera push 1.00 -> 1.035 across the whole scene, back row moves 40% slower (parallax). Pennant outlines flutter.
'Government': fills flood in bottom-up, building by building (govA, govB, govC, govD; 0.35 s wipe each, 0.08 s stagger), plaza mintPale wipes in 0.1 s later. Fills sit 3 px off the ink.
'websites': the four main windows reveal browser chrome: three dots pop (0.04 s stagger, overshoot), address bar draws on (0.2 s), warm glow fades up. This is the 'buildings are websites' reveal.
'in': five back-view citizens slide up 20 px into the plaza with overshoot, staggered 0.06 s; Pip's ear perks.
'four': four pennants unfurl one per building at 1.36 / 1.48 / 1.60 / 1.72 (scaleX 0 -> 1, snap).
'switched': a bold cream power glyph draws onto the sun (0.25 s), replacing the faint one.
'themselves': shutters drop by themselves (no hands, no people): govA 2.80, govB 3.04, govC 3.28, govD 3.44, each 0.18 s with a 6 px bounce. The window glow disappears behind each one.

'off': the sun presses in (scale 1 -> 0.88 -> 1 over 0.3 s, one ink ripple ring), dimWash ramps to 35% in 0.3 s, lamp posts go dark, the three pigeons flap off the wire. Only the sun and Pip stay bright. Pip's ear flares (startled) with a tiny '!' tick.
'Nobody': padlocks pop onto the four shutters (3.76 / 3.86 / 3.96 / 4.06), each with a short glint.
'hacked': Pip trots 30 px to govB's shutter and taps its padlock with his trunk at 4.30; the lock jiggles and holds.
'them': all four locks glint at once. Nothing is broken: windows intact, no intruders anywhere.

scenes.sun: Starts as the plain orange disc carrying a faint power glyph (the loop seam). On 'switched' the glyph inks in bold; on 'off' the disc is pressed like a power button and stays the brightest thing in the dimmed world. Glyph fades out during the S02 transition.
scenes.mascot: Stands on the plaza watching the buildings light up (ear perks on 'in'), flinches on 'off' (ear flares), then on 'hacked' trots over and taps a padlock with his trunk: it holds. Small, bottom-right, never between the viewer and the buildings.

scenes.vo: They were fixing a security bug in PHP, the programming language behind WordPress and about 7 out of 10 websites.

beats.action: 'You'd think': vault is open; bigMagnifier glides in from the left.
'finding': the magnifier sweeps across the bricks (lens magnifies what it passes). As it passes over the crack (16.80) Bit ducks behind a brick edge, then pops back up after it has gone (17.10).
'hard part': the magnifier slows with a heavy wobble; three searchers pop in above ground, magnifiers raised, looking the wrong way.
'right?': Pip turns to camera (the only front view of the film: two dot eyes), one ear raised like an eyebrow, a small '?' pops.
'And': the calendar pops onto the wall with a nail tap. The magnifier exits right.

'14': TIME-LAPSE 18.88-20.32. Calendar pages tear off 1 -> 14 (14 tears, ease-out: fast first, slower last). Sky above ground pulses day/night per year. The tree cycles seasons, searchers walk in and out, the crane arrives, the building above grows a storey, the crane leaves. The cobweb spins across the crack corner. Pip curls up and falls asleep (Zzz) at 19.20. Bit doesn't move.
'nobody': everything snaps still on year 14. Silence beat.
'did': Bit strolls out of the crack and walks across sleeping Pip's trunk; Pip snores a tiny puff and doesn't wake.

scenes.sun: Becomes a clock face on '14': 12 cream tick marks ink in, two cream hands spin 14 laps (in sync with the calendar tears, decelerating), then ticks and hands fade at 20.32 and it is the plain disc again.
scenes.mascot: The fourth-wall beat: turns to the viewer on 'right?'. Then sleeps through the whole 14-year time-lapse, and the bug walks over him on 'nobody did' (rewatch gag: the bug is literally sitting on the elephant).

scenes.vo: Someone has to install that fix on every site, and there are about 22 million copies of PHP out there that could be hit.

Loupe inset x 560-820 y 160-420 in level 4.

scenes.vo: If a site can't update fast enough, the safest thing is to switch it off until it can. That's what those government sites did.
scenes.title: Why they switched off
